candidate.title: TruSeq™ Nano
candidate.scope: The single TruSeq Nano product/library-preparation schematic: double-stranded DNA fragmentation and size selection, end repair and phosphorylation, A-overhang formation, indexed adapter addition and ligation, then denaturation and amplification to a library ready for cluster generation. Adapter forks and opposite-end drawings are molecular structure, not alternative workflows. The biological source and any upstream generation of the input DNA are unspecified. This catalogue figure supports a schematic architecture, not a complete protocol or a primary-paper-defined historical version.

operations.label: Fractionate / Size select
operations.description: Converts the long double-stranded DNA into shorter fragments and retains a size-selected fragment population. The drawing groups fragmentation and selection without a separate intermediate or discard route.
operations.information_effect: Target-derived DNA remains in retained fragments. Size selection limits library representation to that retained population; complete or unbiased recovery of input DNA is not established.

evidence.locator: First downward arrow; Fractionate / Size select caption; shorter duplex product
Long input duplex, Fractionate / Size select arrow, and shortened retained fragment
evidence.rationale: Size selection retains a subset of fragment material. Consequently the downstream library represents retained fragments, without implying complete or unbiased recovery of the original DNA.

operations.label: End repair / Phosphorylate
operations.description: Changes staggered fragment termini into aligned ends and introduces the depicted terminal phosphate groups.
operations.mechanism: End repair and phosphorylation are named; aligned ends and opposing phosphate symbols are shown. No enzyme is specified.

evidence.locator: Second arrow; End repair / Phosphorylate caption; aligned fragment ends with opposing circled phosphate symbols

operations.label: A-overhang
operations.description: Changes repaired fragments into DNA bearing a terminal A overhang at each end while retaining the opposing phosphate-marked termini.
operations.mechanism: Addition of the depicted terminal A protrusions; the enzyme is not identified.

evidence.locator: A-overhang caption and downward arrow; terminal A at upper-right and lower-left of insert; opposing phosphate symbols retained

operations.label: Add Adapters
operations.description: Adds indexed forked adapters to the A-ended fragments, bringing their T-ended interfaces together with the insert ends for ligation.
operations.mechanism: Reagent addition is represented by the plus sign. Covalent joining is assigned to the subsequent Adapter ligation operation.

operations.label: Adapter ligation
operations.description: Joins adapter stems to both insert ends, producing a continuous duplex insert flanked by the depicted forked adapters.
operations.mechanism: Ligation is explicitly named; the drawn A and T protrusions define complementary insert-adapter interfaces.
operations.information_effect: Physically links target-derived DNA inserts to index-bearing adapters and P5/P7 segments.

operations.label: Denature and amplify
operations.description: Denatures and amplifies adapter-ligated DNA into the final straight duplex library with P5/Index 2 and Index 1/P7 ends, ready for cluster generation.
operations.mechanism: Denaturation and amplification are a combined depicted transformation; primers, enzymes and intervening intermediates are not specified.
operations.information_effect: Produces copies while retaining the insert-to-index association. The target-derived DNA insert is the potential sequence readout carrier, while adapter and index sequences are added library features. The two indices identify the indexed library preparation; the figure supplies no cell identity tag or original-molecule counting tag, and depicts no sequencing data output.
